subject: science
prompt:
Take a 2-milligram square of bright orange storage tissue from the center of a carrot root—cells that normally store sugars and never divide again.

Drop this tiny tissue piece into a flask filled with liquid coconut milk, which contains plant growth regulators, and place it on a spinning rotator.

Predict what will happen to these cells after two weeks:

options.text: The cells die instantly because they are severed from the root system.
The cells return to an unspecialised dividing state, form cell clumps, and eventually form roots and shoots.
The cells continue to grow larger as storage cells but never divide.
